findings.claim: ServletExchange.abort() is deliberately lock-free and calls AsyncContext.complete() from stop()/completeAll() or an AsyncListener thread while an SSE drain thread may be inside FlushingStream.write/flush on the same response. The Servlet spec leaves a response write that races complete() undefined; a container that recycles request/response objects on complete (Tomcat-style) could see the drain write on a recycled response. The 'aborted before complete' ordering guards only later writes, not one already in progress. Only Jetty 9.4 is verified and docs/api/servlet.md says so, so no defect is observed today; later waves that add a container (Tomcat/WildFly) will hit it.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-servlet/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/servlet/ServletExchange.java:196-201 (abort -> complete), NaruServe-servlet/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/servlet/ServletEventStream.java:171-180 (completeAll) and 215-231 (writes under synchronized(ex) that abort() does not take)
findings.suggested_fix: If a non-Jetty container is ever verified, complete the AsyncContext from the drain thread (it already completes in drainTask's finally) and let completeAll only set aborted plus a write timeout, or take the exchange lock with a bounded tryLock before complete(). Until then keep the Jetty-only statement in docs/api/servlet.md.
